# [01]{.section-number} Hello, R! {background-color="#3d0251"}

[How do I tell a computer what to do?]{.section-question}

## Console vs script

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Console
Like a **calculator**

Type a command, get an answer straight away. Gone when you close R.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Script (`.R` file)
Like a **recipe**

Save your steps, re-run them any time, share them with others.
:::
::::

<br>

```{r filename="hello.R"}
# Anything after a # is a comment: R ignores it
cat("Hello, penguins!")
```

::: notes
Live code: run `cat("Hello, R!")` in the console. Then File → New Script, save as hello.R, and run it with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter and with Source. Optionally show `Rscript hello.R` in the Terminal tab. Encourage everyone to keep ONE script open all day.
:::

## Your two best friends

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
**Ctrl/Cmd + Enter**
Run the current line (or selection)
:::
::: {.card}
**`# comments`**
Explain *why*, for future you
:::
:::

# [02]{.section-number} Variables & types {background-color="#3d0251"}

[How do I make R remember things?]{.section-question}

## A variable is a labelled box

```{r}
#| eval: true
body_mass_g <- 3750
```

::: {.flow}
[body_mass_g]{.step .light} [←]{.arrow} [3750]{.step}
:::

::: {.center}
Read `<-` as **"gets"**: *body_mass_g gets 3750*
:::

. . .

```{r}
#| eval: true
body_mass_g / 1000
```

::: notes
Show the Environment pane filling up. Shortcut for <- is Alt/Option + minus. Good names: bill_length_mm, not bl or x.
:::

## Four types you'll meet every day

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
**numeric**
`39.1`
:::
::: {.card}
**integer**
`181L`
:::
::: {.card}
**character**
`"Adelie"`
:::
::: {.card}
**logical**
`TRUE` / `FALSE`
:::
:::

<br>

```{r}
class("Adelie") # what type is this?
as.numeric("3750") # convert between types
```

## Asking questions

```{r}
#| eval: true
species <- "Gentoo"
body_mass_g <- 5200

species == "Gentoo" & body_mass_g > 5000
```

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
**Maths**
`+ - * / ^`
:::
::: {.card}
**Compare**
`== != > < >= <=`
:::
::: {.card}
**Combine**
`&` and, `|` or, `!` not
:::
:::

## Spot the mistake

::: {.bad}
`species = "Gentoo"`  ← this **assigns**
:::

::: {.good}
`species == "Gentoo"`  ← this **asks** "is it equal?"
:::

. . .

::: {.bad}
`"3750" + 1`  ← text, not a number: **error!**
:::

::: notes
Run "3750" + 1 deliberately and read the error message aloud: "non-numeric argument to binary operator".
:::

# [03]{.section-number} Data structures {background-color="#3d0251"}

[How do I store more than one thing?]{.section-question}

## Four ways to hold data

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
**vector**
One row of the **same** type
<br>`c(3750, 3800, 3250)`
:::
::: {.card}
**matrix**
A grid of the **same** type
<br>`matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)`
:::
::: {.card}
**list**
A bag of **anything**
<br>`list(species = "Adelie", mass = 3750)`
:::
::: {.card}
**data frame**
A **table**: columns can differ
<br>`data.frame(species, mass)`
:::
:::

. . .

::: {.center .medium}
The **data frame** is the star of the show for the rest of the day ⭐
:::

## Square brackets get things out

```{r}
#| eval: true
masses <- c(3750, 3800, 3250, 3450)
masses[2]
masses[2:3]
```

. . .

```{r}
#| eval: true
df <- data.frame(species = c("Adelie", "Gentoo"), mass = c(3750, 5200))
df[2, ] # row 2, all columns
df$mass # one column
```

::: {.muted}
Counting starts at **1** in R. `[row, column]`, and leave a side blank to get everything.
:::

## Errors are your friend

```{r}
df[, "flipper"]
```

```
Error in `[.data.frame`(df, , "flipper"): undefined columns selected
```

::: {.flow}
[Where it happened]{.step .light} [:]{.arrow} [What went wrong]{.step}
:::

::: {.center}
Read the error. It's usually telling you exactly what's wrong.
:::

# [04]{.section-number} Control flow {background-color="#3d0251"}

[How do I make decisions and repeat myself?]{.section-question}

## `if`: making decisions

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: "|1|3|5"
if (mass > 4500) {
  cat("Large")
} else if (mass > 3500) {
  cat("Medium")
} else {
  cat("Small")
}
```

. . .

::: {.center .medium}
R runs the **first** match, then stops looking.<br>**Most specific condition first!**
:::

::: notes
Live code the classifier, but deliberately write the conditions in the wrong order first (mass > 3500 before mass > 4500), test with 5000, and ask the room what went wrong.
:::

## Quick quiz 🤔

```{r}
mass <- 5000
if (mass > 3500) {
  cat("Medium")
} else if (mass > 4500) {
  cat("Large")
}
```

What gets printed?

. . .

::: {.big .center}
"Medium" 😬
:::

## `for`: do it for each one

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.bad}
Repetitive
:::
```{r}
cat(masses[1] / 1000)
cat(masses[2] / 1000)
cat(masses[3] / 1000)
cat(masses[4] / 1000)
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.good}
Loop
:::
```{r}
for (mass in masses) {
  cat(mass / 1000, "kg\n")
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.center}
Works for 4 penguins or 4 million.
:::

## `while`: keep going until...

```{r}
#| eval: true
fish <- 10
fed <- 0
while (fish >= 3) {
  fish <- fish - 3
  fed <- fed + 1
}
cat("Fed", fed, "penguins")
```

::: {.muted}
Make sure the condition can become `FALSE`, or it runs forever! (Press **Esc** to stop it.)
:::

# [06]{.section-number} Functions {background-color="#3d0251"}

[How do I write code I can reuse?]{.section-question}

## A function is a machine

::: {.flow}
[inputs (arguments)]{.step .light} [→]{.arrow} [function]{.step} [→]{.arrow} [output (return value)]{.step .light}
:::

<br>

```{r}
#| eval: true
mean(c(3750, 3800, 3250))
```

::: {.center}
You've been using functions all along: `cat()`, `c()`, `class()`, `mean()`...
:::

## Building your own

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: "|1|2-7|8"
calculate_mean <- function(values) {
  total <- 0
  count <- 0
  for (value in values) {
    total <- total + value
    count <- count + 1
  }
  return(total / count)
}
```

::: {.flow}
[name]{.step .light} [←]{.arrow} [function(arguments)]{.step} [→]{.arrow} [{ body }]{.step} [→]{.arrow} [return()]{.step .light}
:::

::: notes
Live code it, then call it on penguins$body_mass_g: it returns NA because of missing values. That motivates the next slide.
:::

## When things go wrong

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### 🛑 `stop()`
Halt with a clear error

```{r}
if (!is.numeric(value)) {
  stop("I need numbers!")
}
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
### ⚠️ `warning()`
Carry on, but tell the user

```{r}
if (is.na(value)) {
  warning("Skipping an NA")
}
```
:::
::::

<br>

::: {.center .muted}
`NA` means "missing value". Many functions skip them with `na.rm = TRUE`.
:::

# [07]{.section-number} Reading data {background-color="#3d0251"}

[How do I get my data into R?]{.section-question}

## From file to table

```{r}
penguins_file <- path_to_file("penguins.csv") # a CSV that ships with the package

read.csv(penguins_file) # base R  → data.frame
read_csv(penguins_file) # readr   → tibble ✨
```

::: {.center}
Packages can ship **files** as well as functions!
:::

## Real data is messy

```
Palmer penguins data
Exported for the JGI R course.
A -1 signifies a missing value.

species;island;bill_length_mm;bill_depth_mm;...
Adelie;Torgersen;39.1;18.7;181;3750;male;2007
Adelie;Torgersen;-1;-1;-1;-1;-1;2007
```

. . .

::: {.center .medium}
Three problems: 📝 header text, ➗ semicolons, ❓ `-1` = missing
:::

## Fix it one step at a time

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: "|2|3|4|5"
read_delim(
  messy_file,
  skip = 4, # 📝 skip the header text
  delim = ";", # ➗ split on semicolons
  na = "-1", # ❓ -1 means missing
  col_types = cols(year = col_integer())
) # set column types
```

::: notes
Write the messy file live (see notes, section "Dealing with messy files"), open it in RStudio, then fix it ONE argument at a time, re-running after each. This is the key teaching point of the section.
:::

# [08]{.section-number} Tibbles & the pipe {background-color="#3d0251"}

[How do I ask questions of my data?]{.section-question}

## The pipe `%>%` means "and then"

::: {.medium}
Take the penguins, **and then** keep the female Adelies, **and then** add mass in kg, **and then** sort.
:::

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: "|1|2|3|4"
penguins %>%
  filter(species == "Adelie", sex == "female") %>%
  mutate(body_mass_kg = body_mass_g / 1000) %>%
  arrange(desc(body_mass_kg))
```

::: {.muted}
Shortcut: **Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + M**. You may also see R's built-in pipe `|>`, which works the same way.
:::

::: notes
Build this one line at a time, running after each %>%. This habit is the most valuable thing to model all day.
:::

## Five verbs to rule them all

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
**`filter()`**
keep **rows**
:::
::: {.card}
**`select()`**
keep **columns**
:::
::: {.card}
**`mutate()`**
make **new columns**
:::
::: {.card}
**`arrange()`**
**sort** rows
:::
::: {.card}
**`rename()`**
`new = old`
:::
:::

<br>

```{r}
penguins %>% select(species, island, body_mass_g)
```

# [09]{.section-number} Tidy data {background-color="#3d0251"}

[What shape should my data be?]{.section-question}

## Three rules of tidy data

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
**1. Columns**
Each variable has its own column
:::
::: {.card}
**2. Rows**
Each observation has its own row
:::
::: {.card}
**3. Cells**
Each value has its own cell
:::
:::

<br>

::: {.center .medium}
Tidy data in → easy analysis and plotting out
:::

## Reshaping with `pivot_longer()`

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
<table class="mini">
<tr><th>id</th><th>bill_length</th><th>bill_depth</th></tr>
<tr><td>1</td><td>39.1</td><td>18.7</td></tr>
<tr><td>2</td><td>39.5</td><td>17.4</td></tr>
</table>
:::
::: {.column width="16%"}
::: {.big .center}
→
:::
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
<table class="mini">
<tr><th>id</th><th>measurement</th><th>mm</th></tr>
<tr><td>1</td><td>bill_length</td><td>39.1</td></tr>
<tr><td>1</td><td>bill_depth</td><td>18.7</td></tr>
<tr><td>2</td><td>bill_length</td><td>39.5</td></tr>
<tr><td>2</td><td>bill_depth</td><td>17.4</td></tr>
</table>
:::
::::

```{r}
penguins %>%
  pivot_longer(
    c(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm),
    names_to = "measurement",
    values_to = "mm"
  )
```

::: {.muted}
`pivot_wider()` goes back. `drop_na()` removes missing values. `factor()` sets category order.
:::

# [10]{.section-number} Data analysis {background-color="#3d0251"}

[Which penguins are heaviest?]{.section-question}

## Group, then summarise

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| code-line-numbers: "|2|3"
penguins %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE), n = n())
```

. . .

::: {.center .medium}
[Gentoo]{.gentoo} penguins are over 1 kg heavier on average!
:::

## Filter → group → summarise

::: {.flow}
[filter()]{.step} [→]{.arrow} [group_by()]{.step} [→]{.arrow} [summarise()]{.step}
:::

```{r}
#| eval: true
penguins %>%
  drop_na(sex) %>%
  group_by(species, sex) %>%
  summarise(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g), .groups = "drop")
```

# [11]{.section-number} Plotting {background-color="#3d0251"}

[How do I see what's going on?]{.section-question}

## The grammar of graphics

::: {.flow}
[data]{.step} [+]{.arrow} [aesthetics: aes(x, y, colour)]{.step} [+]{.arrow} [layers: geom_...()]{.step}
:::

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5
#| code-line-numbers: "|1|2-4|5|6"
ggplot(
  penguins,
  aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, colour = species)
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
```

::: notes
Build it layer by layer: data + aes alone gives an empty plot! Then add geom_point, then colour, then geom_smooth. Move colour into geom_point() to show global vs layer aesthetics. Common error: using %>% instead of + between layers.
:::

## Pick the right geom

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| layout-ncol: 3
base <- list(
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_colours),
  theme(legend.position = "none"),
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
)
ggplot(penguins, aes(body_mass_g, fill = species)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 200, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
  labs(title = "geom_histogram()") +
  base
ggplot(penguins, aes(species, body_mass_g, fill = species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "geom_boxplot()") +
  base
ggplot(penguins, aes(species, body_mass_g, fill = species)) +
  geom_violin() +
  labs(title = "geom_violin()") +
  base
```

::: {.center .muted}
Same data, different questions. Swap the `geom`, keep everything else. Then `ggsave("plot.png")` to save it.
:::

## Do longer bills mean deeper bills?

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
ggplot(penguins, aes(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "black") +
  labs(x = "Bill length (mm)", y = "Bill depth (mm)")
```

::: {.center .medium}
Looks like... **no**? Longer bills are *shallower*.
:::

## Look again...

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
ggplot(penguins, aes(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, colour = species)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = species_colours) +
  labs(x = "Bill length (mm)", y = "Bill depth (mm)", colour = NULL)
```

::: {.center .medium}
Within **every** species, longer bills are *deeper*. This is **Simpson's paradox** 🤯
:::

::: notes
This is the "wow" moment of the plotting section. Ask the room to predict before revealing. Lesson: always look at your groups. It comes back in the modelling exercise.
:::

# [12]{.section-number} Models & machine learning {background-color="#3d0251"}

[Can we predict a penguin's weight, or even its species?]{.section-question}

## From pictures to numbers

```{r}
#| eval: true
model <- lm(body_mass_g ~ flipper_length_mm, data = penguins_complete)
coef(model)
```

. . .

::: {.big .center}
+1 mm of flipper ≈ +50 g of penguin
:::

::: {.center .muted}
Formula: `outcome ~ predictors`. Then use `summary()`, `confint()`, `anova()`, `predict()`.
:::

## The modelling toolbox

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
**`lm()`**
A number outcome<br>*"How heavy?"*
:::
::: {.card}
**`glm(family = binomial)`**
A yes/no outcome<br>*"Male or female?"*
:::
::: {.card}
**`lme4::lmer()`**
Grouped data<br>*`(1 | species)` gives each group its own baseline*
:::
:::

<br>

```{r}
lm(body_mass_g ~ flipper_length_mm + species + sex, data = penguins_complete)
```

::: {.muted}
Same formula style for all of them. Add predictors with `+`.
:::

## Machine learning: two flavours

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### 🔍 Unsupervised
*No answers given.* Find the groups yourself.

`prcomp()` · `kmeans()`
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
### 🎓 Supervised
*Learn from examples*, then predict new ones.

`rpart()` decision trees
:::
::::

## Can the computer find the species?

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
scaled <- penguins_complete %>%
  select(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) %>%
  scale()
pca <- prcomp(scaled)
set.seed(42)
km <- kmeans(scaled, centers = 3, nstart = 25)
as_tibble(pca$x) %>%
  mutate(species = penguins_complete$species, cluster = factor(km$cluster)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(PC1, PC2, colour = species, shape = cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = species_colours) +
  labs(colour = "True species", shape = "k-means cluster")
```

::: {.center .muted}
PCA squashes 4 measurements into 2 dimensions; k-means finds 3 clusters **without being told the species**.
:::

## Teach a computer to identify penguins

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
set.seed(42)
train_rows <- sample(
  1:nrow(penguins_complete),
  round(0.7 * nrow(penguins_complete))
)
tree <- rpart(
  species ~ bill_length_mm + bill_depth_mm + flipper_length_mm + body_mass_g,
  data = penguins_complete[train_rows, ],
  method = "class"
)
accuracy <- mean(
  predict(tree, penguins_complete[-train_rows, ], type = "class") ==
    penguins_complete$species[-train_rows]
)
```

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
tree <- rpart(
  species ~ bill_length_mm +
    bill_depth_mm +
    flipper_length_mm,
  data = train
)

predict(tree, test, type = "class")
```

::: {.muted}
Train on 70%, test on the 30% it has **never seen**. Use `set.seed()` so results are reproducible.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.fragment}
Accuracy on unseen penguins:

::: {.big .center}
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * accuracy)` 🎉
:::
:::
:::
